proof.text: Fix $n\geq1$. Put $V_n=\{0,\ldots,n\}$, viewed as the discrete vertex subset, and let $S_n\subseteq\Delta^n$ be the union of the consecutive edges and all vertices. A simplicial map $S_n\times\Delta^r\to Q$ is exactly a family of maps on the edge products agreeing on the intervening vertex products: in each degree these products cover $S_n\times\Delta^r$ and their intersections are the specified vertex products. Fixing every vertex product constantly at $x_i$ therefore identifies its parameter space with $P_n=\prod_{i=1}^nH_Q(x_{i-1},x_i)$. Consequently the required map $\theta_n:H_Q(x_0,\ldots,x_n)\to P_n$ is the pullback of restriction $\rho_n:\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^n,Q)\to\operatorname{Fun}(S_n,Q)$ along that fixed-vertex subspace. This identification is degreewise and commutes with the parameter simplicial operators.

source.place: Notation 4.6.8.1 and proof of Proposition 4.6.8.4: fixed-vertex pullback of restriction

proof.text: The subset $S_n$ is $\operatorname{Sp}[n]$, since its simplices have image in a single consecutive edge (or vertex). Its inclusion is inner anodyne by [lem-cbc-spine-inner-anodyne]. The map $Q\to\Delta^0$ is an inner fibration by the defining horn property of $Q$. For any degreewise injective $k:U\hookrightarrow W$, the pushout-product theorem makes $(S_n\times W)\amalg_{S_n\times U}(\Delta^n\times U)\to\Delta^n\times W$ inner anodyne. A lifting square from $k$ to $\rho_n$ is, by the explicit definition of the functor object, precisely a map from this union to $Q$. Its extension follows from the left lifting property against $Q\to\Delta^0$ and gives the required lift. In particular take $k:\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ for every $m\geq0$. The fixed-vertex condition survives because the vertices belong to $S_n$: the extension already agrees with the prescribed map on $S_n\times\Delta^m$. Thus the pullback $\theta_n$ lifts every boundary, including the empty boundary in dimension zero, and is a trivial Kan fibration in exactly the convention of [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration].

source.place: Proposition 4.1.4.4, product-lifting argument, specialized to Q over the point; compare 01PF Proposition 4.6.8.4

proof.text: The arrow mapping space $H_Q(x,y)$ is exactly $U_Q(x,y)$ in [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], hence is Kan. Products of these spaces are Kan by filling each coordinate horn. To fill a horn in $H_Q(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$, first extend its image in $P_n$ using these coordinate fillers, then use the lifting of the horn inclusion against $\theta_n$: a horn is degreewise injective, so [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] applies. Hence all these multiarrow spaces are Kan; for $n=0$ the fixed-vertex fiber is the point. By [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-homotopy-equivalence], each $\theta_n$ has a simplicial section $s_n$ and a homotopy from the identity to $s_n\theta_n$. Moreover, if two maps $a,b:T\to H_Q(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$ have the same image $u:T\to P_n$, the monomorphism $T\times\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow T\times\Delta^1$ and the constant-in-the-interval base map $u$ produce a homotopy between them over $P_n$. More generally the same lifting theorem applies to $T\times\partial\Delta^r\hookrightarrow T\times\Delta^r$ for any prescribed compatible boundary of such choices. To compose the homotopies below, apply [lem-cbc-kan-mapping-homotopy-invariance] with $u=\mathrm{id}_T$ and $Z=H_Q(x,y)$: the identity induces identity maps on all realized homotopy groups, so $\operatorname{Fun}(T,H_Q(x,y))$ is Kan. Two consecutive homotopies are edges $a\to b\to c$ of this Kan complex; fill $\Lambda_1^2$ to obtain an edge $a\to c$. To reverse an edge $a\to b$, fill $\Lambda_0^2$ with edges $01=(a\to b)$ and $02=1_a$, giving an edge $b\to a$. Thus every finite chain of the homotopies of maps used below yields a single simplicial homotopy, with the indicated parameter $T$ retained.

source.place: Tags 08NM (lemma-trivial-kan) and 08NS (lemma-trivial-kan-homotopy); arrow Kan property from Kerodon 01L5 as recorded in the cited pinch-comparison statement; Kan function complexes from Kerodon 00TN, as stated in lem-cbc-kan-mapping-homotopy-invariance (specialized to the identity)

proof.text: For every monotone $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, restriction gives a simplicial map $\alpha^*:H_Q(x_0,\ldots,x_n)\to H_Q(x_{\alpha(0)},\ldots,x_{\alpha(m)})$. The relations among these maps are literal precomposition identities. Define a representative binary composition by $\mu_{x,y,z}=d_1s_2:H_Q(x,y)\times H_Q(y,z)\to H_Q(x,z)$, ordering the product by consecutive edges. The identity at $x$ is the degenerate edge of $x$. Repeating the first vertex gives a map $H_Q(x,y)\to H_Q(x,x,y)$ whose consecutive edges are $(1_x,f)$ and whose long edge is $f$; repeating the last gives the counterpart with $(f,1_y)$. Each degeneracy map and the corresponding restriction of $s_2$ lift the same map to $P_2$. The relative homotopy construction of step 3 identifies them over $P_2$. Applying $d_1$ gives the left and right unit homotopies, since the long-edge restriction of either degeneracy is the identity on $H_Q(x,y)$.

source.place: Construction 4.6.8.9 and Proposition 4.6.8.11; degeneracies repeating the first or last vertex

proof.text: Write $T=H_Q(x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3)$ and let $f_{ij}:T\to H_Q(x_i,x_j)$ be restriction to the $ij$ edge. The $012$ face and $s_2(f_{01},f_{12})$ lift the same consecutive-edge map; step 3 gives a homotopy $\mu(f_{01},f_{12})\simeq f_{02}$. Insert it in the first variable of $\mu(-,f_{23})$, and compare the $023$ face with $s_2(f_{02},f_{23})$, to obtain $\mu(\mu(f_{01},f_{12}),f_{23})\simeq\mu(f_{02},f_{23})\simeq f_{03}$. The $123$ face gives $\mu(f_{12},f_{23})\simeq f_{13}$; insert this in the second variable of $\mu(f_{01},-)$, and compare the $013$ face with $s_2(f_{01},f_{13})$, obtaining $\mu(f_{01},\mu(f_{12},f_{23}))\simeq\mu(f_{01},f_{13})\simeq f_{03}$. All these are homotopies with parameter $T$. Reverse the second chain and join the chains by the Kan-function-complex horn fillers of step 3. Precomposition with $s_3:P_3\to T$ gives the associativity homotopy with parameter the full product of three arrow spaces. The coherent composition data are the complete family $H_Q(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$ with all ordinal restriction maps of step 4: each spine restriction $\theta_n$ is a trivial Kan fibration and the ordinal identities hold strictly. Explicitly, a family of choices over a parameter $u:A\to P_n$ is a lift through $\theta_n$; a compatible prescribed $r$-boundary of such choices is a map $A\times\partial\Delta^r\to H_Q(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$ over $u\operatorname{pr}_A$. Step 3 extends it across $A\times\Delta^r$. For a fixed string, take $A=\Delta^0$: the choice fiber is nonempty by $r=0$, and it lifts every boundary. Applying the trivial-fibration homotopy theorem of step 3 to this fiber over a point gives a section and a contraction. These relative fillers and the strict ordinal identities are the higher comparison homotopies asserted by the statement; no compatibility of independently chosen binary sections is assumed.

source.place: Remark 4.6.8.7 (Segal category), Corollary 4.6.8.8 and proof of Proposition 4.6.8.12; relative choice extensions use Stacks 08NM

proof.text: A simplicial functor $F:Q\to Q'$ acts on every $H$ by postcomposition. For each monotone $\alpha$, the equality $F\circ(h\circ(\alpha\times1))=(F\circ h)\circ(\alpha\times1)$ shows that all face, degeneracy, spine and long-edge maps commute with $F$. This is naturality of the coherent composition data itself. If binary sections in the two quasicategories have been chosen independently, $Fs_2$ and $s'_2(F\times F)$ are two lifts in the target with the same consecutive edges, hence are homotopic by step 3; their higher comparisons use its relative boundary extensions. Thus the asserted naturality is coherent, as is necessary when simplex fillers are nonunique.

source.place: Notation 4.6.8.1, Remark 4.6.8.7 and Construction 4.6.8.9; functoriality of all restrictions

proof.text: Let $f:x\to y$ and $g:y\to x$ have inverse-triangle witnesses $w_x\in H_Q(x,y,x)_0$ and $w_y\in H_Q(y,x,y)_0$ whose long edges are $1_x$ and $1_y$. Compare $w_x$ with $s_2(f,g)$ and $w_y$ with $s_2(g,f)$ over their respective spines by step 3 and apply the long-edge maps. This gives paths $\mu(f,g)\simeq1_x$ and $\mu(g,f)\simeq1_y$. For any $z$, define $f_*(a)=\mu(a,f)$ on $H_Q(z,x)$ and $g_*(b)=\mu(b,g)$ on $H_Q(z,y)$. For the whole parameter spaces, the associativity and unit homotopies of steps 4-5 give $g_*f_*(a)=\mu(\mu(a,f),g)\simeq\mu(a,\mu(f,g))\simeq\mu(a,1_x)\simeq a$ and $f_*g_*(b)=\mu(\mu(b,g),f)\simeq\mu(b,\mu(g,f))\simeq\mu(b,1_y)\simeq b$. Define $f^*(b)=\mu(f,b)$ on $H_Q(y,z)$ and $g^*(a)=\mu(g,a)$ on $H_Q(x,z)$. Then $f^*g^*(a)=\mu(f,\mu(g,a))\simeq\mu(\mu(f,g),a)\simeq\mu(1_x,a)\simeq a$, while $g^*f^*(b)=\mu(g,\mu(f,b))\simeq\mu(\mu(g,f),b)\simeq\mu(1_y,b)\simeq b$. The middle homotopies insert the inverse-witness paths into the corresponding variable of $\mu$; step 3 joins each chain into a simplicial homotopy. For the right-pinched convention, use the homotopy equivalences $j_{a,b}:\operatorname{Map}_Q(a,b)\to H_Q(a,b)$ of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] and choose homotopy inverses $r_{a,b}$. A precomposition or postcomposition map $v:H_Q(a,b)\to H_Q(c,d)$ is represented in this convention by $\widetilde v=r_{c,d}vj_{a,b}$. For its inverse $w$, the composite is $\widetilde w\widetilde v=r_{a,b}w(j_{c,d}r_{c,d})vj_{a,b}\simeq r_{a,b}wvj_{a,b}\simeq r_{a,b}j_{a,b}\simeq\mathrm{id}$, and $\widetilde v\widetilde w=r_{c,d}v(j_{a,b}r_{a,b})wj_{c,d}\simeq r_{c,d}vwj_{c,d}\simeq r_{c,d}j_{c,d}\simeq\mathrm{id}$. These homotopies can be joined using the Kan-function-complex conclusion of [lem-cbc-kan-mapping-homotopy-invariance] with identity source map and the Kan right-pinched target. Thus both mapping-space conventions have the asserted inverse homotopies.

title: Coherent composition from multiarrow spaces
statement: Use simplicial sets, quasicategories and functor objects as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a quasicategory $Q$ and vertices $x_0,\ldots,x_n$, let $H_Q(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$ be the fiber of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^n,Q)\to\operatorname{Fun}(\{0,\ldots,n\},Q)$ over the constant vertex diagrams $x_0,\ldots,x_n$. For $n\geq1$, restriction to consecutive edges is a trivial Kan fibration $H_Q(x_0,\ldots,x_n)\to\prod_{i=1}^n H_Q(x_{i-1},x_i)$, where trivial Kan fibration means lifting all boundary inclusions $\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, $m\geq0$. The face and degeneracy maps give composition, identities, associativity and their coherent homotopies, natural in simplicial functors. Inverse edges with inverse-triangle witnesses therefore induce inverse homotopies on precomposition and postcomposition maps. Here $\partial\Delta^n$ denotes the union of the faces of $\Delta^n$, with $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$.

source.place: Corollary 4.6.8.5, Remark 4.6.8.7 and Construction 4.6.8.9 in Subsection 4.6.8 (01PF), Composition of Morphisms.
